title: texualselect regressions due to change in how TextualSelect is treated in the compiler

labels.name: easy
labels.description: a one / two  liner type of thing that anyone can do in short order. also see "fairly easy"

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

body:
### Describe the bug

When compiling the `sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql.Insert` statement with a `select_from(text("SELECT ..."))` (_cf._ MVCE below) and the `.on_conflict_do_update()` method to add the , the compilation fails with the error (_cf._ stacktrace below)

### Case 1

```python
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, MetaData, Table, Text, text
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import dialect as pg_dialect, Insert

meta = MetaData()
bar = Table('bar',
            meta,
            Column('id', Integer),
            Column('attr', Text),
            Column('foo_id', Integer)
            )
s1 = text('SELECT bar.id, bar.attr FROM bar').columns(bar.c.id, bar.c.attr)
s2 = (Insert(bar)
      .from_select(list(s1.selected_columns), s1)
      .on_conflict_do_update(index_elements=[s1.selected_columns.id],
                             set_={'attr': s1.selected_columns.attr},
                             )
      )
print(s2)
print(str(pg_dialect.statement_compiler(pg_dialect(), s2)))
```


### Error

### Case 2

```py
from sqlalchemy import Column, insert, Integer, MetaData, Table, Text, text
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import dialect as pg_dialect
from sqlalchemy.dialects.mysql import dialect as mysql_dialect


meta = MetaData()
foo = Table('foo', meta, Column('id', Integer))
bar = Table('bar',
            meta,
            Column('id', Integer),
            Column('attr', Text),
            Column('foo_id', Integer)
            )

s1 = text('SELECT id FROM foo').columns(foo.c.id)
s2 = (text('SELECT bar.id, bar.attr FROM bar WHERE br.id IN (SELECT id FROM baz)')
      .columns(bar.c.id, bar.c.attr)
      )
s3 = insert(bar).from_select(list(s2.selected_columns), s2)
s4 = s3.add_cte(s1.cte(name='baz'))

print(str(pg_dialect.statement_compiler(pg_dialect(), s4)))
print(str(mysql_dialect.statement_compiler(mysql_dialect(), s4)))
```



### Versions

- OS: Ubuntu/ Debian
- Python: 3.9.10
- SQLAlchemy: 1.4.32
- Database: postgresql
- DBAPI (eg: psycopg, cx_oracle, mysqlclient): psycopg2 2.9.3


### Additional context

The fix is pretty simple: instead of using `insert_statement.table.c` one has to use `insert_statement.selected_columns`. Though I guess this would require the addition of non-regression test for the future. Hopefully, one can be derived from the above example. 

I feel guilty as I am pretty sure those changes come from this issue #7760 I reported earlier. I didn't take the time to check the fix before the 1.4.32 release.
